tasks.short: Watch the patient and ventilator at the bedside, read vital signs and blood gas values onto the flow sheet, compare them with targets and trends, and consult the physician if adverse reactions occur.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist monitors the patient's physiological responses to therapy at the bedside
Respiratory therapist writes vital signs and arterial blood gases on the flow sheet
Respiratory therapist compares values with targets and trends
Respiratory therapist consults with the physician if adverse reactions occur

tasks.design: The bedside monitor, ventilator and blood gas analyser send their values to the electronic patient record ({OTHER}), so the therapist validates values instead of writing them on a flow sheet. A trend screen shows values against the physician's targets. Watching the patient and consulting the physician stay with the therapist; the trend screen shows values and does not advise treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were read from screens and written onto paper or typed into the record.
tasks.enabler_now: Device integration sends monitor, ventilator and analyser values to patient records.
tasks.still_hard: Artefacts from movement or loose sensors produce false values.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a patient tire on the ventilator before the numbers show it.
tasks.altitude: The therapist validates values instead of copying them.

reach.learn: Whether trends are complete at rounds.

evidence.claim: Device integration can send monitor, ventilator and blood gas values to the patient record.
Decision software is usually MDR class IIa or higher; a display of values without advice is kept out of that scope here.

assumptions: Boundary: from the therapy running to the physician consulted; changing orders is the physician's step and outside.
Input contract: devices connected to the record; fallback is the paper flow sheet.
Bedside watching and consulting do not change.
The therapist validates every value before it counts in the record.
research_questions: Do transcription errors in the record fall?

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist marks artefact values as invalid.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a ward with few ventilated patients; high: an ICU with many devices.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the prescription and patient record, draw the arterial blood sample, run it on the blood gas analyser and note the values, and assess the patient's condition.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist reads the prescription and reviews patient information
Respiratory therapist draws the arterial blood sample
Respiratory therapist measures arterial blood gases on the analyser and notes the values
Respiratory therapist assesses the patient's condition

tasks.design: Orders, recent results and the problem list show on one screen in the patient record ({OTHER}) instead of being looked up in several places. The blood gas analyser, scanned with the patient's wristband, sends values to the record, so they are not written down. Drawing blood and assessing the patient stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sat in several screens and analyser values were copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient records combine views; analysers send results by wristband scan.
tasks.still_hard: Sample errors such as air bubbles still need the therapist's eye.
tasks.human_edge: Matching a blood gas result to how the patient looks and breathes.

reach.learn: Whether blood gas results are visible sooner.

evidence.claim: Blood gas analysers can send results to the patient record after a wristband scan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the therapy order to the condition assessed; treatment changes are outside.
Input contract: analysers connected to the record; fallback is writing values down.
Drawing blood and assessing do not change.

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist scans the wristband before each sample run.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few blood gases; high: an ICU with many samples per shift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read blood analysis results, check them for critical values, release routine results to the physician, phone critical results with read-back, and note that results were relayed.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist reads blood analysis results from the analyser printout
Respiratory therapist checks results for critical values
Respiratory therapist relays routine blood analysis results to a physician by phone
Respiratory therapist phones critical results to the physician with read-back
Respiratory therapist notes that results were relayed

tasks.design: Analyser results land in the patient record ({OTHER}), where fixed critical-value rules set by the laboratory flag results outside limits. Once the therapist has checked the results, routine ones are released to the physician's worklist with a notification instead of a call. Critical results are still phoned with read-back, and the record logs who was told and when.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every result was read from a printout and phoned.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient records flag critical values by rule and notify physicians of new results.
tasks.human_edge: Saying a result in a way that makes a busy physician come now.
tasks.altitude: The therapist calls only for critical results.

reach.learn: Whether routine results are seen in time.

evidence.claim: Patient records can flag results outside fixed limits and notify physicians.
Calamities go to the IGJ without delay, so missed critical results must be traceable.

assumptions: Boundary: from the analysis done to the relay logged; acting on results is the physician's step and outside.
Input contract: critical limits set by the laboratory; fallback is printout and phone.
Physicians read the worklist in about the time a call took; no added physician time.
s5 is part of keeping therapy charts, which sibling task 29-1126.00:404 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: Results per shift, and the share that is critical.
research_questions: Are routine results seen by physicians within the agreed time?

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist checks that released results were seen.

approvals.approved_version: The results as checked by the therapist in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many critical results that still need calls; high: mostly routine results.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check physicians' orders against protocols, check equipment, oxygen and alarm settings, correct colleagues and patients on safety rules, and report safety incidents.

steps.what: Respiratory therapist checks physicians' orders against protocols to ensure careful adherence
Respiratory therapist checks equipment, oxygen and alarm settings
Respiratory therapist enforces safety rules with colleagues and patients
Respiratory therapist reports safety incidents on the paper form

tasks.design: Order checks in the patient record ({OTHER}) flag doses and settings outside the unit's protocol by fixed rules, so the therapist reviews flags rather than reading every order against the protocol book. Incidents are reported on the hospital's electronic incident form. Checking equipment and enforcing rules stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders were compared with paper protocols and incidents reported on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based order checks run in Dutch care systems; incident forms are electronic.
tasks.still_hard: Too many flags make staff ignore them.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a senior colleague to stop when a setting is wrong.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates by rule.
Calamities go to the IGJ without delay.

assumptions: Boundary: from the therapy order to the incident reported; incident analysis is outside.
Input contract: protocol limits set by the unit; fallback is the protocol book and paper forms.
Checking equipment and enforcing rules do not change.
research_questions: How many flags are true problems?

incremental.description: Respiratory therapist reports false flags to tune the rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few orders; high: an ICU with many order changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The respiratory therapist keeps watching patients, drawing blood, assessing and enforcing safety; copying values, routine calls and paper forms shrink.
skills_to_grow: Validating device data in the record
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time at the bedside.
